utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Before I invite Madam Registrar to call the case, I'd like to verify whether the videolink with the United Nations Detention Unit is functioning well. Mr. Stanisic, I can see you. Can you hear me? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are nodding yes, could you perhaps speak a bit louder so that I know for sure that I can hear you as well. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that -- let me just check. Could you please speak a few more words so that I'm certain that I can hear you in the microphone, please. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I receive now translation, so that means that our interpreters can hear you. Mr. Jordash, has the telephone line been tested so that Mr. Stanisic, if he needs to contact you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There isn't a phone apparently. I just checked with the technician and apparently because it's a very temporary situation a phone isn't available, which I wanted to flag up as a potential issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because I was used to a telephone line to be there. Mr. Stanisic, if at any point in time you would like to consult with Mr. Jordash, and, Mr. Jordash, of course the same is true for you, then please make that clear so that there will be a confidential way of communicating and we would, if need be, we would interrupt the proceedings for that purpose. These are all the practicalities. Madam Registrar -- THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Jordash, I did understand from your response that you do not oppose against proceeding even when the telephone line is not available constantly?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if there are no other procedural matters, the witness could be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Registry further explores about the availability of telephone lines in need, if need be. Mr. Weber, yesterday you indicated that you needed 15 minutes. I said that you would certainly not be granted more than 30 minutes which is not an invitation to use 28 minutes, but rather 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and if it assists, I am going to resume with the document that we left off on, which is 65 ter 6270.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have that then already on our screens. Now, I've forgotten one final thing, that is Rule 15 bis, Judge Picard is unavailable for urgent personal reasons. I announced already yesterday that we might have to sit Rule 15 bis, Judge Gwaunza and myself, we have -- we are satisfied that it's in the interests of justice to proceed in her absence. So, therefore, we ordered that the hearing of the case continue in the absence of Judge Picard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, dobro jutro I should say, perhaps. Good morning, Mr. Novakovic. I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony is still binding, that is that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the Prosecution could please have page 3 of both the B/C/S and the English versions of this report for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First of all, good morning, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We are going to continue with the document that we left off with yesterday, which is the report involving the six tasks that were being performed by the JATD during Operation Pauk. Sir, if you could please read part 6, the sixth task of this report entitled "Conducted Sniping Operations." The section here continues over the next page, so if you could please let us know when you need the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Serbian DB was conducting sniping operations by day and night during Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely know nothing about that. I've not seen anything about that before. This is the first time I see it in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that the Serbian DB carried out a sniping operation against a house and a hotel using a submachine and a 90-millimetre hand-held OSA launcher, Osa launcher?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This report ends: "A list of the special equipment issued follows:"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the original document and page 4 of the English translation for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, according to this list, the Serbian DB issued Raja Bozovic an automatic pistol with 160 rounds, night vision goggles, a sniper rifle, and a laser pointer. Legija on this list was also provided with a sniper rifle. Based on your assignment did you know that the Serbian DB was issuing weapons like this?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The opinion that you expressed in your comment chart indicates Jovica Stanisic and the Serbian DB were gathering information and did not have the capacity or logistics to provide materiel assistance. Based on what I've shown you, do you agree that this opinion is not accurate because you were not in a position to know this information?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Defence have shown me these documents which show that operations were undergoing sometime in August 1994, and I provided comment on that information. Sniper rifle doesn't mean that there was an operation undergoing. I do not have that kind of military logic to be able to comment upon this. As far as I can see, these are things that were issued in mid-November, equipment and ammo issued in mid-November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to make sure that we would then understand your evidence correctly. Is it correct then that your comments were solely based on two documents that were shown to you from August 1994 and that you don't have knowledge of events that occurred from November onward in Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided comments on four documents, those that were shown to me and that are contained in the binder, and I provided my comments on the contents of the documents. As for the information as to what was going on and what was subsequently noted here, I didn't know anything about that. I've not seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 6270 into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P3024, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. No need to have it under seal, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution re-tenders the four 1992 reports on the White Eagles. These were 65 ter 6263 to 6266 and we would tender those under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the numbers would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 6263 will receive number P3025. 6264 will receive number P3026. 6265 will receive number P3027. And 6266 will receive number P3028, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3025 up to -- before, I -- Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, my reaction may be a bit belated. Some of the documents, especially 6263, have been redacted. There has been redaction with regard to the addressee, the signature, and I believe that there are other documents in the group of the same kind and that's why I object to their admission, because I think we should wait and we should be provided with the unredacted versions of those documents before we are able to admit them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Prosecution possessed the unredacted versions, those are the ones that we would have uploaded. We don't have them. We asked that they be admitted based on the evidence that has been offered by the witness and, of course, we are willing to inquire about obtaining unredacted versions of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We are -- I don't know if Your Honour remembers the conversations we had many weeks ago about unredacted documents. For Your Honours' information, we are about to file a Rule 54 motion in relation to our documents which remain redacted. We would invite the Prosecution to do precisely the same with the documents that they rely upon. We would submit a simple inquiry is clearly not enough. What they need to do is what we have been urged to do which is to file a motion pursuant to Rule 54.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you would include a motion under Rule 54 to be included in your efforts to get unredacted copies, Mr. Weber, if you don't have, if you are unsuccessful in getting them in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in all fairness to the Republic of Serbia, I believe we should first request and see if they would provide them, but then if for some reason that there's trouble with it, yes, of course we'd follow through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you communicate with Mr. Jordash to see what efforts have shown to be successful or unsuccessful so as not to waste time and as to expedite matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the Prosecution may be able to -- I don't know what the situation is with the Stanisic Defence, but we are in contact and I believe we do have occasion to speak with them even in the near future to attempt to resolve this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we also had the experience that sometimes you were unsuccessful in these efforts, but, Mr. Jordash, every effort is included. Yes. Then whether or not we finally would admitted, if we would not receive the unredacted copies is still to be seen, we'll mark them for identification at this moment. Of course, the evidentiary value is not always totally destroyed if there are redacted copies, although the Chamber has insisted until now always on receiving unredacted copies. For that reason, for that reason alone, we will mark for identification, under seal, P3025 up to and including P3028. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution indicated that it would return with further information on Exhibit P3018, a proposal for awards dated 6 May 1996. This was 65 ter 1D5061. The Prosecution further reviewed the names and submits there are no names that require protection and the document can become public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the status of P3018 therefore changes into public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Lastly, Your Honours, as I stated at the outset of this witness's evidence we have a number of outstanding requests to the government of Serbia with respect to materials. We did receive some preliminary information during the course of the examination of the witness which I did try to formulate some general questions to the witness on. However, we did not have those materials and we have not received them yet. They appear to contain relevant information. This may likely cause the witness to be recalled in the future. In addition to this circumstance, we stand by our submissions regarding the lack of disclosure and notice for several aspects of this witness's evidence. We will further look into these matters and evaluate the circumstances and any prejudice to the Prosecution. With that in mind, the Prosecution would ask that the Chamber instruct the witness not to discuss his testimony with anyone pending a recall. With that, Your Honour, the Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against the request from Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Petrovic, apparently you are sharing the view of Mr. Jordash. Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, at the same time -- well, first of all the Chamber will give the instruction as you asked us to do. You said you have not received documents, you have some information. You are expected at this point in time to do everything you reasonably can do, and of course if circumstances, including the material you have received, do not allow for certain further examination, then of course we will consider a request for a recall of this witness, but please be aware that what you can do now you are supposed to do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I fully understand that, and the Prosecution did try to do its best. We received very minimal, a paragraph of some general information from -- that was provided through an opportunity with BIA, there's a large quantity of documents and we have not obtained those documents. So I was severely limited in some basic information that I could provide without having that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see your point and it is accepted. I'll give the instruction to the witness before he leaves this courtroom. Mr. Petrovic, any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd ask for your leave to put several questions to Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Novakovic, Mr. Petrovic will have some further questions for you, listen carefully and please answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And make a break between question and answer, but also between answer and question, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We will do our best and I speak also on behalf of Mr. Novakovic. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Petrovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Novakovic, as of the setting up of the 2nd Administration in 1992 through to the end of 1993, is it true that Marko Lazovic was the head of the 2nd Administration in that period, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware that after Marko Lazovic, it was Zoran Mijatovic who became head of the 2nd Administration in 1994?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know that Franko Simatovic had never been appointed as head of the 2nd Administration, rather he was acting chief of the 2nd Administration; right?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Witness, a short question regarding the criminal procedure as it was applied in Serbia at the time. Members of the Ministry of the Interior were authorised to file a criminal report. Would there follow any criminal proceedings thereafter is something that is out of their hands; right?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Bear with me for a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, at the time you worked for the Uzice centre, did you ever receive information about extremists and their activities in Bosnia and Croatia from the services in Bosnia, Croatia, the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and Republika Srpska, was there any sort of communication in place?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 1992 and?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your departure from the Uzice centre.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it having happened in the Uzice centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at Exhibit P3019.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is confidential document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, yesterday you looked at this document while being examined by my learned friend. It is an Official Note by RDB members. There is mention made of an automatic rifle be provided on the order of Bojovic, et cetera, et cetera. This is my question: This is intelligence obtained from the conversation with Djurovic. Was that information checked? Is what is contained here what Djurovic said and what the official noted and of which the official did not ask that it be verified?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely so because there is no reference made to a source other than Djurovic and the interview with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And nowhere in this note is there a mention made of the information having been checked anywhere; right?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, professionally speaking, what is the importance of the note? What follows once such a note has been drawn up? What is required for a piece of information to be checked and used further on?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professionally speaking, this is initial information that needs further processing based on the means available. Based on whether this sort of activity is recurrent and whether there is urgent need of it being discontinued, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at 1D5062, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We ask one follow-up question exactly in relation to this document, the note about Mr. Djurovic. You told us that the document doesn't say anything about verification of the information contained in this Official Note. Do you have any personal knowledge whether at a later stage verification took place or not, or are you just unaware and are you commenting on what you see in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is preassigned number D429, Your Honours, and temporary under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the document which comes on the screen now, not to be shown to the public. I'm still talking about the Djurovic document. Do you have any personal knowledge on whether in the follow-up whether further processing the information was verified or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As can be seen in the heading of that earlier document, these are problems along the third line of work and I was supposed to be commenting on it. I was charged with counter-intelligence affairs, whereas this subject matter was dealt with by my colleagues who were charged with extremism and I had nothing to do with that. So I would say that I assume that the information was checked subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you have no personal knowledge about that, so we are just focusing on this one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Witness, please, look at the document. You had occasion to see it over the past couple of days. Do you know that under the constitutional system of the Republic of Serbia, the Presidency of the Republic of Serbia as an institution existed until the adoption of the 1990 constitution?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell you with any certainty what the year was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well. If I were to tell you that this is a form that was produced in an earlier period and which was used for the payment of per diems, would you agree with such a statement?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could, yes, I could agree. It was yesterday or the day before yesterday that I said that I am no expert for financial matters. I'm not familiar with forms of this type. What I can tell you is that I presume on the basis of the heading that the per diems were paid out in accordance with the decision of the Presidency of the Republic of Serbia. And of course, it does not state when this decision was taken by the Presidency, but it was paid to PJM members.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. Can you clarify for us, the PJM within the system of the interior of the Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia fell under public security and their competence, did they not?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't know if everyone else can hear Mr. Stanisic speaking. I wonder if he ought to be told that his voice can be heard just in case he discusses any confidential information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can't hear him at this moment because whatever he would say would first go to the interpreters, but perhaps it's good, Mr. Stanisic, that you are aware that the microphone in the room where you are is constantly open. I see your lips moving, although I do not hear what you say, but please be aware that it might be caught by the microphone before you. Now, I also see that the microphone sign in the left bottom corner -- yes, Mr. Stanisic, in addition to what I just said, I would like to inform you that you cannot call Mr. Jordash but if you would like to consult with Mr. Jordash, you can ask for a communication through the videolink and then Mr. Jordash will call you on an extension which will be given to you, Mr. Jordash, by Madam Registrar. Perhaps you are aware of it already, but otherwise, the number is available. Internal phone line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have one question left for this witness and for that I would need us to move into private session or closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into -- private session will do?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, have you testified before this Tribunal earlier, and if so, in what case?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified in 2008 in the case against the accused Milan Lukic. I was called to appear by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you testify as a Prosecution witness in that case?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my only request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to flag this. This was something that if raised earlier, the Prosecution would have had further examination on. So I just wanted to note that for the record, that this questioning, even out of the gate here, could trigger further questioning by the Prosecution or we'd ask leave for further questioning on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see what happens. At the same time, Mr. Weber, the Chamber was not informed about any earlier testimony, I think, of this witness before this Tribunal. Of course it sheds some light on exploring the background of the witness, et cetera, if you have used him as a witness before, if you have called him as a witness before, I take it that you have interviewed him and that, for example, things like the existence of criminal records, et cetera, has been verified at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There would be some circumstances that we would raise and this is outside the scope of the cross-examination that was by the Prosecution. It was not raised during that. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that was not the point I was -- what I was doing, as a matter of fact, is I was establishing that due to contacts the Prosecution will have had earlier with this witness, that perhaps there is already more information about him known to the OTP such as, I take it that you don't call a witness without knowing even about whether he has a criminal record or not, that you have certainly explored something about this witness, wouldn't it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness -- the Prosecution will not describe as co-operative beforehand. He didn't -- refused to meet with us, the information that we had was limited to Official Note and one other report with respect to Milan Lukic, and he didn't meet with us when he came to The Hague and he was called, and he asked to be a Chamber witness, and those were the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, of course, is not a complete answer. You say we had difficulties in exploring the background, may be true, may not be true, but you certainly have made efforts and what you could obtain without the co-operation of the witness, I take it that you would have obtained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was very limited. We asked -- it was very limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is yes, although it was very limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I just wanted to ensure that there's no misconception. Whilst the witness did refuse to meet with the Prosecution, he also refused to meet with the Defence. His wish was to be a, as he described it, an impartial Chamber witness, but in the end what he was a Prosecution witness. So that I think is important to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to say that he was called by the Prosecution, to that extent he was a Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, the characterisation as a Prosecution witness if someone refuses to talk with the calling party prior to giving testimony is not a normal Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there are limits in there. Of course, if a party calls a witness, a Chamber witness is -- we usually leave it to the parties even if there are difficulties first to call witnesses, and usually Chamber witnesses are considered those witnesses called by the Chamber where the parties, for whatever reason, finally decide not to call that witness, whether or not co-operative, but that's usually what we qualify as Chamber witnesses in this Tribunal. The attitude of the witness, and that's, I think, what Mr. Weber draws our attention to, was one that he would not -- he would prefer not to be affiliated to one of the parties in the case but rather to come without such preparation with one of the parties or any affiliation with one of the parties. That's how I understand the observations made by Mr. Weber, although finally it was the Prosecution who called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, and he was led by Mr. Groome in direct examination and relied upon by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we accept what Mr. Jordash said, that's accurate as to the circumstances and, really, if there's any cross on this, we don't dispute what was just said. Those were the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I take it that from my observations, not being contradicted, that I have a proper understanding of what both Prosecution and Defence has submitted. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you provide a signed statement to the representatives of the OTP of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they invited me to provide a statement, I signed the statement and my only request with regard to my appearance at the trial was not to be a witness either for the Prosecution or the Defence. I wanted to be the Chamber witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Weber, this is a new element which comes up. Could you give us an indication as to whether this would trigger all kind of additional questioning or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It would not if the parties were to agree that the witness did not appear voluntarily to provide a statement, that he was subpoenaed to do so and the scope of the subpoena indicated that it was limited to a discussion of specific documents in the Lukic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any dispute about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No dispute about that, perhaps, though, the Prosecution would, perhaps not now, but at least indicate therefore what investigation they did conduct into this witness having decided to call him, having located him and having sought a subpoena, that implies a certain level of inquiry which may be important in the future in terms of any application to recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would, as a matter of fact, I would invite the Prosecution to keep all the material available, but as long as there's no such request, I would say let's not anticipate -- let's prepare for such a situation but let's not yet at this moment do this exercise and rather wait until you've made up your minds on a potential recall. Would you agree with that, Mr. -- because I immediately responded to Mr. Jordash without giving you an opportunity to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution is willing to proceed in that manner. We would disagree with what Mr. Jordash just said in terms of the opportunity that we were provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic -- it is queuing before the microphones at this moment. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one remark with regard to your previous question. I cannot say anything about the nature of the relationship between the witness and the OTP. I just have a comment. The witness has obviously shown a level of co-operativeness with the Prosecution just based on the fact that he provided a statement and signed it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, may I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, whether the glass is half full or half empty, Mr. Petrovic, that is something we could discuss for the next century. The Prosecution has emphasised that they needed a subpoena to get him there for limited purposes for a statement, so co-operative attitude or non-co-operative attitude, let's think about the glass half full or half empty. That's clear. Mr. Jordash, you are -- any further questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, Mr. Jordash will now further examine you. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It was suggested to you by my learned friend by the Prosecution that if during Operation Tomson the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We are in private session apparently, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we shouldn't be in private session. Can we return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It was suggested to you by the Prosecution that if during Operation Tomson you came across the name of somebody in the JATD, then any investigation into that person for extremism or the like would come to a halt. Are you aware of any record or central database or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please just have -- is that a direct quote?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first listen to the question and then you have an opportunity to object. Mr. Novakovic, don't answer the question yet. First Mr. Jordash will phrase his question, then Mr. Weber will say something, and only after that you are invited to answer or perhaps not to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you aware of any record or central database or something similar which you had access to at that time which recorded all the names of those in the JATD? Did you have access to any such database?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the question actually stands independent and fine without the reference to the submission that was earlier, so I have no objection to the question as posed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the introduction was a reference to the evidence that triggered you to put this question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The position that the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any database, any such database, Mr. Novakovic, did you or did you not have it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, and if there was any such database, it was not accessible to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, on the screen, P3027.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to deal with the suggestion that the DB didn't take action against the White Eagles until 1994. We can see this document which you've been shown, the 27th of August, 1992, and as we know, it's a document recording an Official Note of an interview with information about the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go, please, to the last page. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And we can see there at the end of the document: "We informed the CJB about the announced extremist actions of the White Eagles from Priboj, in order for the appropriate measures to be taken." In light of this Official Note of interview and the information within, what might such appropriate measures have encompassed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we don't know yet. There a risk of speculation. Perhaps you phrase the question in such a way first, concrete, whether the witness has any knowledge about what kind of action was envisaged, and then perhaps in what general terms, what kind of -- so we go from the concrete to the more general question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You hadn't seen this document before, but having seen the document, do you have any independent recollection of the information contained within and what, if any, measures were taken by the public security in relation to the information in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document yesterday. However, what I see at the end of the document is something that shows that the state security sector informed public security sector about certain activities, and then the latter would step up their activities by way of patrols, interviews with the population, longer duration of stay in the area that is indicated as a possible hub of terrorist activities. Here there's reference to four facilities owned by Muslims, a village with the Muslim population and so on and so forth. So this is the only way that the state security sector could prompt the public security sector to patrol the area as much as possible and to surveil the area as much as possible while pursuing their operative activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, I just want to be clear about making the distinction between what you know happened in relation to the White Eagles, and what you are inferring must have happened from your knowledge of documents such as this with information that was being passed to the public security. So firstly, in August of 1992, did you have -- sorry, let me start that again. Did you have any knowledge of what measures were being taken by the public security in August of 1992 in relation to the White Eagles and their activities?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any specific information about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- Mr. Jordash, there's another matter that came to my mind, please correct me whether I'm wrong, I'm also addressing Mr. Weber, the issue about action taken only in 1994 in relation to matters that happened in 1992 was about -- and please correct me when I misunderstood the issue, I'm just defining the issue, nothing more. I'm not expressing any opinion or judgement about it. But I think the issue was that the Prosecution sought to establish that where the reports indicated that crimes had already been committed, that no investigation, prosecution, adjudication was started until 1994. Whereas the document we are looking now at this moment is about information that crimes or at least certain activities may develop. And I see -- I'm not saying that it's not relevant what you are talking about, but that there's a distinction between investigating crimes that have been reported as already been committed, compared to activities which are announced and where you take measures whatever those measures will be. I see a distinction there because you introduce this matter now as something, that's actually the way you introduced it, to more or less challenge what the Prosecution sought to establish that no action was taken until 1994. Whereas I see that the circumstances in which action was taken is different in the two situations, the one crimes already reported to have been committed, and here activities, but whether I should call them crimes or not I leave that open, but still to take place and I think even scheduled for the 28th of August, where the document dates from the 27th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether my understanding of the issues -- I'm not going to stop you, but whether my understanding of the issues to be different in this respect, whether you share that or whether you do not share that because then I have to ask myself why I don't understand the issues raised by the parties. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes the Chamber is correctly interpreting what the Prosecution was using the evidence for. The only second component to it that we would add is not only the knowledge of the fact that crimes were committed, but then when action was taken, the action was not taken against those crimes but for different crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But it was the follow-up of crimes already committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could I just -- it's probably me, but just if I could be clear what the Prosecution are alleging. Are the Prosecution alleging that the White Eagles committed crimes in 1991 and 1992 and 1993 and the DB was aware of those crimes and failed to take action, does that summarise the Prosecution position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Defence is raising Operation Tomson as one of its defences. In rebuttal of Operation Tomson, Mr. Jordash has made a number of submissions as to the way in which this was implemented, how it was implemented, so we are offering that evidence to rebut what the Defence has put forward in terms of the DB acted -- showed certain concerns, that these concerns were egalitarian between a bunch of different ethnic groups, that they acted as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's another aspect of what you raise, but I think that your main rebuttal was if this was the reaction, it was not only incomplete, but it was also two years after the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the events, the reporting on the events was about events that had taken place already, whereas here we are looking at a report on events still to take place so therefore the measures could hardly be to investigate the crimes because if there were any crimes, they were not yet committed, they were just announced. That's what I wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your "yes" I take it that you agree at least with the analysis of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- and I hope that the position will become clear or clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's just return to this document briefly, Mr. Novakovic. When you look at the Official Note or unofficial note such as this were there observation that the writer of the note informed the public security about announced extremist actions, are you able to just give us a quick rundown, a quick list of what such an author might anticipate the public security would do, or would have done at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Talking from practice, when the public security sector in charge of the relevant area is informed about possible threats, the public security sector then steps up control measures, patrols, interviews with people, checking information provided to them. All that means that the territory will be controlled in the upcoming period when activities are expected to take place. Here reference is made to Operation Tomson. I would like to say something about that. Operation Tomson was carried out by the Republic of Serbia on the territory of Serbia. The document that we referred to yesterday dealing with Operation Tomson, the one shown to me by Mr. Weber, is an amalgamated document that speaks to the state security sector activities from 1992 through 1995. In that document, you can see what was done and what needs to be done in the future, and these are separate documents and in general terms, all these documents have been incorporated into the amalgamated document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- my time is limited so I want to just focus you if I can. Thank you for the information, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have 1D03220.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just take your time to look at this. I don't think you've seen it, or maybe you have, but we haven't shown it to you. Do you -- have you seen this before? Have a look.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Just take a few moments to glimpse through it and see what it is. 15th of May, 1991, Zajecar state security, 3rd Administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While the witness reads, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, foundation. At this time the witness has never seen the document before. We are now discussing a new document in a different area and region and this should have been led in chief, and I did not discuss certain events. I focused on this witness's administration and experience, security sector and we would object to proceeding in this way. Using the document in this fashion may be leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you don't know yet what the question is. Perhaps Mr. Jordash wants to establish that the witness can read, isn't it? That is still a possibility. Or that -- let's object to questions when we have questions. Mr. Jordash, I do not expect you to establish that because that was clear already.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You can see there in the -- I'm particularly interested in the comment in the last paragraph relating to the White Eagles. And let me just focus you on the following: "Earlier we obtained the information about an alleged plan to form a volunteer detachment in the Majdanpek area, so now we do not rule out the possibility of receiving the idea to form such a detachment. Especially now by Milanovic and Radivojevic or Radojevic, because on his return from" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you really need to pronounce it, the names are so similar. The first one you referred to Zoran Radivojevic or Radojevic because otherwise the transcript will be very difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "Because on his return from Borovo Selo, Misko Milanovic told our agent that they had received the task of finding two volunteers each to take part in any new action. This assumption is supported by the information we have about the existence of a number of supporters of the Beli Orlovi, White Eagles, youth organisation of the SCP Serbian Chetnik Movement in the Majdanpek area. It cannot be categorised as a paramilitary unit now, but at the initiative of extremists, they may go on to arm the organisation." Is that information anything that you are able to comment on, that the view of the State Security Service in May of 1991, that the organisation of the White Eagles was not armed at that point?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not seen this document before. I can see that it was drafted by the Zajecar centre, that it was sent to the 3rd Administration, and they're referring to a document from the office the secretary by which this information was sought. This points to the fact that during that period of time that there were organisational measures being dealt with, but in the last sentence it is stated that this is a youth organisation of the Serbian Chetnik Movement but that it was still not a paramilitary formation, but that it was possible that they were dealing with the arming of extremists. I'm basing this on the information that was available to the centre at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you have any information of a similar kind in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a subject of interest in the territories of Priboj and Prijepolje where the activities were going on when the activities of the White Eagles were launched in our area. The White Eagles appeared everywhere in every area as --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when they appeared in 1991, how did they appear, in which sense --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please, first of all, the appropriate way of dealing with the matter would have been that you ask the witness whether he knows anything about the activities of the Beli Orlovi youth organisation which is, of course, we are not focusing until now on the youth organisation, so first to explore that. Now, let's try to remain concrete. What happens if the football hooligans enter Belgium? I mean, these kind of questions, please focus and aim at obtaining concrete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know when the White Eagles started to arm themselves?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the territory of my centre, in the territory of Priboj where their activities was the most intense, they started arming themselves in 1992, when the war started in the territory of Bosnia. That's my opinion. That's as much as I know about the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I tender this as an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have no objection for it being marked for identification pending some further information on origin. We would like to see the RFA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about the origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: At this point no, but I can have our Case Manager --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it will be marked for identification. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be D448, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D448 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Jordash, I'm looking at the clock. I do not know, it's not mainly to limit your time, but on whether one extended session by five or seven minutes would do or whether we need to continue after a break anyhow?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I would like another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another 20 minutes. Then I think you are stepping beyond the time I gave you yesterday, but we'll verify that during the break. You need a break anyhow. We'll have a break and we'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00, but before doing so, I would first like to verify with Mr. Stanisic whether at this moment there's any need for consultation and whether there are any other wishes as far as he is concerned. If you nod no, Mr. Stanisic, then I'll put that on the record, and if you confirm that you need further consultation, I'll put that on the record as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters can't hear Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear you. Could you speak closer to a -- I think the microphone is switched off, from what I see on my screen. Could it be switched on first of all. On the left bottom of my screen it says "far" and then there's a microphone with a -- it's stricken through in red. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have tried on several occasions to communicate with the Defence, but I did not succeed. I don't know whether you can hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, I can hear you now, and apparently there is a problem with the microphone being closed on your side of the communication. I suggest that Mr. Jordash will call you under the number that will be given to him by Madam Registrar. And, Mr. Jordash, is there any way that you or your team could keep an eye on the microphone, because earlier we said the microphone is open, please be aware that everyone can hear you, which apparently led to closing the microphone. But of course if you want it to be in touch with us, then you should open it again because otherwise the interpreters do not receive any audio from the UNDU. Mr. Stanisic, is it clear that if you want to contact Mr. Jordash, that you should take care that the microphone is open and, otherwise, I'm not constantly looking at the video from the UNDU. Therefore, perhaps someone could keep a close eye on any attempts by Mr. Stanisic to reach Mr. Jordash. I, for the time being, leave it, Mr. Jordash, to a telephone conversation you may have with Mr. Stanisic during the break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00, but only after I have urged the parties to provide the material for the videolink on Tuesday in relation to DST-052 by today to the Registry because it has to be copied, it has to be taken to the place of the videolink, and if you provide it at any later stage, there is no guarantee that it can be processed and copied and therefore be used during the videolink. Then there is one other matter for which we'll go into private session immediately after the break. We resume but then in the beginning for three minutes without the witness and we will move in private session at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, did you have an opportunity to consult, to speak with Mr. Stanisic and raise any additional matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No -- I did communicate with him. He provided some instructions and I'm ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just raise one issue, which is just for Your Honours's information in relation to the Rule 54 application that we will file I think today. One of the requests is for the DB's annual reports which we hope will deal with some of these subjects and assist with clarifying some of the issues about what the DB did and when they did it. Unfortunately, until we receive those, we are somewhat hampered in relation to, for example, these issues in terms of getting the full picture about what the DB was doing in relation to the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you for the first time ask for these annual reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Off the top of my head I don't know, but I know it was several years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Several years ago, yes, that's what one would expect to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, it's a pity that you have not sought at any earlier stage an order to be issued because we are close -- coming closer and closer to the end of your case and, of course, the Chamber is concerned if you are unable to -- to investigate relevant material and to present it to the Chamber if that research would make you believe that it is relevant material. It's still very late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, Mr. Jordash will now put some more questions to you and most likely will be done in half an hour approximately. So it will be a short session. Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, please keep your answers as brief as possible so I can get through the material as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please can we have on the screen 1D01006.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You mentioned before the break about the White Eagles starting to carry weapons sometime in 1991. When in 1991, beginning, middle, or end?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was towards the end of 1991. I think, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And as far as you are aware, was action taken by either the public security or the state security in relation to that carrying of weapons within Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of Serbia, anyone found carrying weapons, especially long-barrelled weapons, military ones, would be detained. That was our practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just have you pay some attention to the document on the screen. 2nd of August, 1995, Operation Tomson report from the Sremska Mitrovica state security. And the first two paragraphs are pertinent to this subject. The paragraphs note two essential facts. One, that the White Eagles seem to, according to this report, morph or change into these other formations such as the Serbian Chetnik Movement, and, two, that in the early stages of the war, the White Eagles avoided bringing weapons into the FRY and did not expose themselves as a paramilitary organisation or formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't know if there's a question, but this is leading. He is summarised a document and is paraphrasing it and asking a witness whether or not he agrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I've not asked a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then now think well about your question, Mr. Jordash, because you might be in trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask the witness whether he has a comment to make upon this particular report and its contents, which I think is common practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although always first explore with the witness, we are talking about a specific time-frame, we are talking about an area, isn't it. There is -- whether he knows about the report. We first explore what the witness knows without just reading the report and say I think it will be right or I think it will not be right. Apart from that, of course, much of this information of a very general character and that requires quite a bit to establish what the witness -- whether the witness really is able to have an overview over all the events, whereas we had a lengthy examination of the witness on what he knew exactly about what happened in the next street and in the next village. So, therefore, please first explore, but let's proceed at this moment as you suggest. Any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, any comment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this document from the centre of the state security in Sremska Mitrovica, which is close to the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia. The war had begun in Croatia much earlier than in Bosnia. That is characteristic that the White Eagles appear on the ground and they are armed especially -- exactly at the moment when the war begins. They are using this occasion to go to the war as volunteers and then come back to Serbia with their weapons. That's my general comment about the distinction between these two areas, the centre in Uzice and the centre in Mitrovica. I worked in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Were you able within the Uzice centre to, at any stage from 1991 to 1995, define who was in the White Eagles, what the membership was, the numbers, the identities of the members?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period it was established and the amalgamated document that speaks to the Operation Tomson defines this precisely and it says that in 1994 the work of that organisation was broken. The commander of the White Eagles was the subject of our intensive work and that implied significant measures on the ground. It also mentions other individuals. That document specifies what was done in 1992, 1993, 1994. It's a document that speaks of the achievements, the results of our work, and further directions we intend to pursue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you able to identify now the time when the DB, the Uzice centre had a clear picture of who the White Eagles were and the identities of the members? Are you able to recall roughly which year that information was obtained in some depth with some detail?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not working on this myself. It could have been 1993 when the activities of these people became known in some detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. If you say it could have been 1993, that means, as you started your answer, that you are not working on the matter, you have no detailed knowledge about it, and what could be, Mr. Jordash, is not what assists the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, let's just put this exhibit to the side. I just want to ask you about a finding in the Lukic judgement, paragraph 78, the judgement from this court, and paragraph 78 notes that there has been no convincing evidence presented to the Trial Chamber as to Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic's membership of the White Eagles or Avengers or any linkage between the White Eagles or Avengers and any of the crimes with which Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic are charged. So the finding of this court was that the Prosecution haven't established Lukic was a member of the White Eagles. Were you aware of that finding?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. First of all, leading and also this is very misleading way of doing this. There is lots of evidence presented in the Lukic case which this witness is not privy to and to present all that that's related to that and then have the witness comment on that, he would need much more additional information, so at this time we would object to using that in this way. We believe that if the Defence does want to seek adjudication of facts that were found in different judgements, they have a vehicle to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution have made much suggestion that the state security didn't do enough in relation to prosecuting Milan Lukic as a member of the White Eagles. It's significant, we would say, that the Prosecution in this court were unable -- notwithstanding a trial lasting nearly two years and all the resources at their fingertips were not able to establish Milan Lukic's membership of the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me read again your question. Well, the only question that's put to you at this moment, would you please restrict your answer to that, whether you were aware of a finding in a judgement, paragraph 78, about the membership of Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic of the White Eagles? Are you aware of that finding in a case that was brought against these two persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, that's an answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll leave it there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me move to another subject, Mr. Witness. Pauk, you've been shown evidence relating to the DB's alleged contribution to the military operation Pauk. Are you aware of any criminal purpose that existed in relation to the objectives for Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Criminal?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, do you know if there was, from what you observed in your presence there, from your information gathered, whether their objectives of Operation Pauk included any criminal purpose?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that from my point of view. I saw that those activities were unfolding in order to get the refugees to return from the RSK to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You've been shown evidence of the participation of some members of the JATD in Operation Pauk. Are you able to provide any evidence concerning the number of corps, military corps, which took part in Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I did not have access to such information. I did not have any insight into military matters or contacts with the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you observe any crimes being committed during Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any contact with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. The last subject. I want to ask you about Ilok. You were shown a document purporting to be the -- part of or the personal file of a man the Prosecution say was called or nicknamed Pupe, Nikola Pupovac, and the Prosecution suggest he is a member of the Serbian MUP, special purposes unit in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen please, 1D05095.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just the way it's been going, I do know what this exhibit is. It's not on their exhibit list but it does come from the Prosecution. I ask that a foundation be laid with what his knowledge of Ilok is before the document is even being shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Foundation for any questions, yes, well, Mr. Jordash, I -- although Mr. Weber is on his feet usually very early, which is sometimes good, we know what the witness said about what he learned about a person by the short name Pupe during an interview and I think the witness also told us that that is all he knows. So therefore, if you want to put documents to the witness and to ask him to further consider or comment, perhaps it would be good that you, knowing what the document is about, first explore whether the witness has any knowledge on the matters contained in that document apart from reading it and then gaining for the first time in his life the information you want to ask questions about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the way in which the Prosecution dealt with this was to put to the witness Mr. Pupovac's alleged personal file -- I see Mr. Weber is on his feet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but he certainly will allow you to finish your sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what we'd like to do is put to the witness various other personnel files which relate to 1992 Ilok special purposes unit MUP Krajina, not MUP Serbia, and go through the same process that the Prosecution went through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, isn't it true when the Prosecution tried to establish that Mr. Pupovac was a member of that, we stopped the Prosecution doing that and said that it was inappropriate where the witness doesn't know anything else to draw conclusions from documentation that -- is my recollection right that I in rather strong wordings said that this is not what would assist the Chamber, to ask the witness to interpret and to evaluate pieces of evidence he was totally unaware of, and where the only thing he knew is that Mr. Lukic once referred to Pupe. Now, the same would apply to you. The Prosecution has tried to do that. I think that the Chamber has in rather strong words said that this is really what we did not expect a party to do. We would not expect you to do a similar thing either, and if you say, well, it's unfair because they started already doing it and we don't get even a chance to make that mistake, then I would -- you have to accept that if it was useless for the Prosecution to do, it will be useless for you to do as well. Again, this is a kind of a general warning not knowing what kind of questions and what kind of material you are going to put to the witness. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, one comment and potential solution. With respect to this, there's a big difference between the Prosecution leading something and the Defence now having to in an open-ended fashion direct examination elicit evidence, so what we did in a leading fashion we'd also add would be improper now to do and suggest to the witness. Possible solution: There are documents that the Defence have uploaded, individual selected documents from entire personnel files of ten different individuals. We believe that it would be fine if the Defence wanted to upload the entire personnel files of each of these ten individuals in the -- with complete translations because there are documents that further put into the context the selected documents by the Defence, that would ensure that there is no misleading nature to taking a individual document out of context for the other documents of the file. And then with respect to these ten individuals, it would be necessary to properly place these ten individuals into the context to have two additional files, and those would be the files. So we would not oppose if the Defence wanted to do that and introduce evidence in that fashion, the admission of the files in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I see that you are, where we yesterday said that the way in which you proceeded was not assisting the Chamber, that you are making an utmost effort to assist Mr. Jordash, but let's see what Mr. Jordash thinks about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think the Prosecution -- well, I'm grateful for the suggestion. I hope they don't mind if we decline. The Prosecution's approach has been throughout this case to select documents from the DB files and put them forward in support of their case. It's not been the practice to put every single document that they have, and that's the way they've proceeded, and what my learned friend is doing now is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to cut it short. Mr. Jordash, I get the impression that what you'd like to do is to bring to the attention of the Chamber that there are documents in the personnel files of persons or a person where that person is linked to an organisation of an other state than Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now, of course this Chamber had heard evidence on how you can be subordinated to one organisation or to another, and that sometimes at least some witnesses told us that that was also linked to the mission you were on. I mean, I leave that open on what evaluation is. If you want to establish that, do we need the witness for that, or could you agree with Mr. Weber that such a document or two or three or four documents where you want to draw our attention to because it gives a heading which links the person to another one, if the witness knows anything about it, fine. If not, why not establish that such documents do exist and that you may interpret those documents in a different way than Mr. Weber does. That's another matter. But that's apparently what you want to bring to your attention. From my observation only, you may understand that it is already now brought to my attention that they exist. If you agree on that, we'll have a look at it and that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree. There's no need to make an elephant out of a mosquito. We can just indicate to Your Honour what the documents are in response to the Pupovac document. We don't actually probably need the witness. We can bar table them with Your Honour's leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would believe the most efficient manner to do that is that if they are seeking individual documents from these files, we would like the Chamber to be privy to the entire ones. So if we could select additional documents in there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, Mr. Weber says if you extract one document from such a personnel file, that you might miss the whole of the picture. You want to draw our attention that at least such documents do exist and are found this those files. Would you oppose to then for the context -- then submit the whole of that file in which at least one or perhaps more documents are found which certainly go in a direction away from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the -- I'll need to check this, but I think the answer will be we won't object. What we do object to, though, is the shifting position of the Prosecution who up until now when its favoured them, they have been happy to select documents, but now that it favours the Defence, they want the whole document, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You can ask for contextualisation and then we would approach it in a similar way, but of course, most important at this very moment is, can the witness add anything to that or not. I am afraid that he might not be able to do it. If you have any reason to believe that that is different, then I suggest that you put questions to the witness in relation to that perhaps before even showing the document, inquire whether he has any knowledge. If he has any, then the document can be put to him, I would say. And if the witness has no knowledge, to find another way of bringing to the attention of the Chamber that where the Prosecution is linking Mr. Pupovac to the -- THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] May I help you, Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Probably best we do it confidentially, Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand that if Mr. Stanisic would like to -- THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] May I help you, Jordash?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, I give an opportunity to Mr. Jordash to give a call to you and you will then be able to decide what you want to bring to the attention of Mr. Jordash and whether Mr. Jordash finds it wise then to bring it to the attention of the Chamber. You have an opportunity to call. Madam Registrar has the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I say this as well, Your Honour, that as far as I'm concerned, Your Honours' approach is the better one. I don't intend to put the documents to the witness. We'll bar table either the documents we want or we'll go along with the Prosecution's suggestion and put in the whole file, but we won't detain the witness on this issue anymore, and that will be, subject to Mr. Stanisic's instructions, the end of my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I think it would be wise to verify whether those are Mr. Stanisic's instructions. I give you a moment to make that phone contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, I think I'll have to use that phone there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since you are speaking English, don't speak too loud, Mr. Jordash, or use a phone somewhere else in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll try here so that the Court isn't disturbed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll keep my earphones on so we'll not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But will Mr. Weber, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He will put his earphones on as well. Mr. Weber, isn't it, we are closing our eyes for whatever Mr. Jordash tells ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can hear Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Jordash, I do understand you are now going to call Mr. Stanisic. It's important at the beginning of your telephone conversation that you emphasise that Mr. Stanisic should switch off the microphone which links him to this courtroom, otherwise we would be privy of all the details of your conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
