utterances.text: We wait for a second until Mr. Jordash returns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I would like to ask one question and I'd like to ask the witness the question concerning the nature of the document, the format of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I take it that you've expressed some concerns about using documents, but here it's apparently a matter of possible authenticity issue or -- yes, and I think that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We agree, they are authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but whether you agree or whether you disagree with Mr. Jordash will become clear if we have heard his question and perhaps the answer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that's going to be the case, we ask that the question be posed in a very open-ended fashion and that any comments be restricted to not contain anything about the substance of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash has heard your request, and Mr. Jordash is aware that he is using a document for the first time to that extent finds himself in examining the witness in chief. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have please on the screen 1D05095.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I am sorry, but I do not think that this was one of the ones that we even got notice of. I have 1D5083 to 1D5092.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We have provided notice, but just to save time let's go then to 1D05083.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just have it noted for the record that at this time we are not being put in a position to use other materials in these files due to the timing and the fact that the other materials are not uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: These were notified to the Prosecution yesterday. And they are uploaded and they come from the Prosecution's own files.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence had an opportunity to conduct a very lengthy direct examination over four hours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any specific question in relation to this -- we'll consider any request for one or two additional questions in relation to this. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, you've been in the -- you were in the DB for in excess of 20 years, and what I want to ask you about is the format of this document and whether you've seen this type of document and its heading and its format during your time in the Serbian DB, emanating from the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We ask the witness now whether he is familiar with, whether he has seen before this or similar documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've never in my life seen a document like this before. I think -- I see this refers to the MUP of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Forget for a moment its actual contents. Have you seen the format before? Does this document -- sorry, let me start that again. Is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please be clear when you are talking about format. Format is usually a standard form of a document. Now, you say apart from the content, there's not much specific and standard in here in you've never seen such a document before, so you should be very clear on what exactly you then mean by format, because if you say it's typewritten with the name of the authority to which it relates to the left top corner, I could tell you that I've seen a million documents of such kind. Whether there's any specific format in that at all is the first question that came to my mind. This witness has never seen this or any similar document before in his life. Could you please, if you have any additional questions, be very focused on what exactly you mean and to phrase your question with well-defined terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. May I just consult with Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is a document which purports to be a request to be admitted into a service. Have you ever seen a request to be admitted into the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I have, but that has nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the document you've seen, requests to be admitted into the DB service, could you describe how they differ from the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- that's already leading. You suggest that there's a difference. They could be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The witness said he had nothing to do -- I'll rephrase the question, if Your Honour thinks its leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The documents that you've seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- you said you have seen requests to be admitted in the DB of Serbia. Could you tell us when did you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Primarily in the last stage of my work in the service. The last period of my work in the sector before retirement. Before that, people were not admitted based on requests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in the later stages you say they were admitted upon request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the last stage. First of all from the establishment of the security information agency onwards until -- before that it was the service who would usually contact potential recruits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you said "from the establishment of the security information agency onwards," could you give that a date, a time-frame, month, year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Recruiting younger people in the BIA's interest in expanding began with a democratisation of society, that would mean from 2001 onwards. When open announcements on the BIA website were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say requests to be admitted into the service in relation to Serbia, you know that from after the year 2000 and not from any earlier year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you that requests as a way to apply for a vacancy is something that I know about from 2001, when vacancies were announced openly on the website, and then people were able to contact the agency in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was the procedure, if you know, in 1992 for recruitment of members of the DB?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure was that the service itself identified persons in whom they had an interest. They would be interviewed, and after the interview, the conclusion would be made if the candidate was fit for working in the service. And if the service decided that the candidate was fit, the candidate was asked to write a CV.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, I've got nothing further. Thank you, Mr. Novakovic. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, have the questions by Mr. Jordash triggered any need to further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would like to show one document based on the last questions and also ask the witness if he is also equally unfamiliar with something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there may be a lot of material where we could ask the witness whether he is unfamiliar with it, then I have a -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 6272, page 12 of the B/C/S original and page 14 of the English translation. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Weber:

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sir, could you please take a look at the document that's before you, and my question directly relates to the formatting, not the content, but are you also unfamiliar or are you familiar with a heading or format used like this by the Serbian DB based on your experiences through your employment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm absolutely not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would just -- I believe the rest of it the witness isn't needed for. We would ask that Prosecution 65 ter 6272 and 6271 be considered in conjunction with any submissions related to the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't know the full contents of this document, I haven't had a chance to review it. We haven't been notified of it. We would like the opportunity to see it first before advancing a position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would also make our position clearer in detail which we are not able to do now, but we have a general comment about what we call personnel files here. There is a major dilemma whether these are indeed personnel files or collections of material that were developed and kept for an entirely different purpose. We will discuss this later on in the case, but for the moment I would like to make this distinction in terminology clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we have no definition yet of what exactly a personnel file is but it's certainly a collection of documents in relation to a person, and whether there's then a personnel file and who put it together, that's a matter that the parties have ample opportunity to further discuss. Let me see, have numbers -- has a number been assigned to the previous one. Do you tender that one, the one where the witness said he had never seen that before --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I take it that you would like to have the other two documents to be in evidence as well, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we'd ask that the -- for the other document that was used by the Defence that the entire file be uploaded. We'd have no objection to the admission of it with the entire file, and then we would ask for 65 ter 6271 and 72 to be admitted to further put that into context, and in all fairness to the Defence, I believe they should have an opportunity to review the files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's keep matters short at this moment. What I'm going to do, I'm going to ask the Registrar to assign a number to the one document taken from what you say was a personnel file, we mark it for identification, we ask the parties to seek an agreement on what contextualisation they would like to have. If you agree on it, we'll then consider to have the one document replaced by the series or the whole file in accordance with your agreement, and at the same time I'll ask the Registrar to assign numbers to the other two documents. So we -- at this moment there are three individual documents which will be assigned numbers, they will be marked for identification, and whether that first one will later be replaced by a broader file or a series of documents, we'll hear from you whether you could agree on that or not. If not, the Chamber will decide on whether the whole of the file will be admitted in addition to the one document filed, or a selected series of it. We'll see that, but that's how we are going to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, without detaining the Court, there are 375 files altogether and we are at this point in time considering how best to present that material to Your Honours without overloading Your Honours but presenting a fair picture of what those files contain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the extent the parties can agree -- could agree on what would be a representative sample of such files, of course, we would welcome any such agreement and then we'll decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the three documents which we have seen, the first one was the request for being admitted into the RSK unit was number, could you please tell us the 65 ter number and then that number assigned to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think it was 1D05083.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D449, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that should be under seal, not under seal. I think we dealt with it in open court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, strictly speaking, because there's the name of somebody who I don't know might have ended up working for some intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not know either, so it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the Prosecution two 65 ter numbers, it's the entire files not just the document, just to make the Chamber aware of that. And the document that was shown was okay to be broadcast but we would ask that the 65 ter numbers be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so now there is confusion about the parties at what 1D05083 stands for, that's only the one document. Yes. And then we have two other documents and you are hereby instructed, Mr. Weber, as matters stand now, to upload either under this number or on any other number the two documents, the requests for admission, but now to the Serbian organisation, to say so, separate for the time being, waiting for any agreement between the parties, you may revisit the question and have the entire file uploaded if there is no agreement with the Defence. So you reserve that right. But those two documents and do we know which one exactly they are?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've used the specific page of 6272 in court which was page 12 of the original B/C/S and page 14 of the English in e-court, so we can replace under a point 1 that specific page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page -- Madam Registrar, is it sufficiently clear to you although not uploaded as such?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'll try to repeat. So the page 12 in original, 14 in English translation of current 65 ter 6272, that will be uploaded as 6272.1, 65 ter number, will receive a number, P3029, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. And that one page needs to be under seal, not to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It does not need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it does not need to be under seal. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to the other one, the Prosecution is -- there's one entity being discussed and another entity being discussed and the other file puts into context the two. So there's a document in that that is not being offered because it's an admission for active service so we would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the witness -- I take it that this witness will not be able to tell us anything about it. Apparently the parties want to draw to our attention the various type of documents found in files of which Mr. Petrovic says it's unsure whether we could call them personnel files, but at least they are in there, and that the issue you want to draw our attention to is that it's how to enter a service from what state, what is the method in being employed, and the second is in what organisation, was it a Serbian organisation, was it an SRK organisation, in which the people were employed, the people to which these files relate. That's the issue. And then I take it that apart from any authenticity challenges, et cetera, that the parties could reach an agreement to inform the Chamber in such a way that it assists us in whatever direction but in better understanding what documents are there, what they say, and of course then we'll have to evaluate what findings they -- what kind of findings they would justify the Chamber to make. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, we have -- we appreciate very much that you came to The Hague, that you've answered all the questions you have, apart from that you have -- well, you have been a witness not only telling us your testimony but also a witness of what happens in this court on all kind of procedural matters. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home, luckily and hopefully even before the weekend rather than after the weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With your leave, I would like to address the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, please you may briefly address the Court but since I do not know what you are going to say, it might be that at a moment I say please stop it. Please proceed. * THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] It is about my previous stay here in The Hague in 2008 because there was some discourse with this regard just awhile ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was a matter I think we dealt with in private session and I think it's not appropriate. If you -- I'd rather leave it out. Unless you say there is a something important for us to know, then we move into private session first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Inter*pretation] I would kindly ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, we are in private session. What would you like to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be literally short. In 2008 I was invited by the district court in Belgrade, court for war crimes, and this was done through the agency that I worked on. They wanted me to come to the premises of the court in Belgrade for an interview. I voluntarily responded and I went to the office, and on two or three occasions, I spoke to the inspectors' representative representing the Prosecutor's Office. What I'm saying is that I went voluntarily in keeping with the decision on the co-operation between Serbia and The Hague Tribunal, the only request that I had at the time was this: I -- they drafted a statement, I signed the statement and my only requirement was to testify not as a Defence or a Prosecution witness, but as a Chamber witness. And this is the only truth about the whole event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that we have dealt with this matter before. There seems to be no disagreement among the parties about what in that respect happened. Some of the terms are a bit unclear of when you are a Chamber witness, I think we have set out the matter in sufficient detail, there's no dispute about it, so I would like again to leave it to that. We move again into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Novakovic, again, I wish you a safe return home again. We adjourn and we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before we adjourn, Mr. Novakovic, you may have noticed that the Prosecution does not exclude for the possibility that they would ask you or to call you again to testify. That's uncertain at this moment. But out of caution, I would like to instruct you that until that matter has been clarified, so either you are recalled or you receive a message that you will not be recalled, that up until that moment, that you would not speak with anyone about your testimony as you've given it before the Tribunal or any testimony still to be given in the future. So please don't communicate or speak about it. We -- that's clear to you now. I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn and we'll resume on Tuesday -- my agenda is slightly different now, Tuesday will be the 10th -- 11th of October at 9.00 in the morning -- someone has changed my agenda programme in my computer so I'm a bit lost. Tuesday, the 11th of October, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom II.
